description: Enable IPv4 packet forwarding (router/NAT functionality). Required for `iptables -j MASQUERADE` to work, and what `docker -p` requires on the host. Disabled = host won't route packets between interfaces.
Enable SYN cookie protection against SYN floods. 1 = engage when SYN queue overflows; 2 = always. Default 1 — almost always leave on.
Time held in FIN_WAIT_2 before forced cleanup. Lowering helps clear orphaned half-closed sockets faster (high-load proxies sometimes set 30).
Allow reuse of TIME_WAIT sockets for new outbound connections (only safe with timestamps option). 2 = loopback only (safer default since 4.12).
Max half-open connections (SYN_RECV) per listening socket before SYN cookies kick in. Raise on heavy connection-rate servers.
Cap on TIME_WAIT sockets system-wide. Beyond this, TIME_WAIT entries are dropped immediately — risky with delayed-segment scenarios.
Ephemeral port range for outbound connections. Widen on hosts opening many concurrent outbound conns to a single dest:port (e.g. proxy to backend). Format: low high.
TFO mode bitmask. 1 = client, 2 = server, 3 = both, 4-9 = various with-cookie modes. Default 1 (client only).
Idle time before keepalive probes start. Per-socket override via TCP_KEEPIDLE.
Interval between keepalive probes. Per-socket: TCP_KEEPINTVL.
Number of failed probes before connection is reset. Per-socket: TCP_KEEPCNT.
TCP receive buffer auto-tune: min default max bytes. SO_RCVBUF setsockopt overrides (and disables auto-tune for that socket).
TCP send buffer auto-tune: min default max bytes.
System-wide default. Available algorithms in net.ipv4.tcp_available_congestion_control. Common: cubic (default), bbr, reno, dctcp.
Enable PMTU probing fallback (when ICMP needed-fragment is blocked). 1 = enable on PMTUD blackhole detection; 2 = always enable.
RFC 1323 window scaling. Disable only if a buggy middlebox strips the option.
RFC 1323 timestamps. Required for tcp_tw_reuse, PAWS protection, accurate RTT.
Selective ACK (RFC 2018). Improves recovery from multiple-segment losses.
SYN retransmissions before connect() gives up. With default ~127s total timeout.
Retries on established connection before giving up. Default ~15min total.
Retries on connection that the local end has closed. 0 = use system default 8.
0 = save TCP metrics (cwnd, ssthresh) per-destination; 1 = disable. Saved metrics speed connection ramp-up to known-good destinations.
Reset cwnd to initial after RTO-equivalent idle. Disable for keepalive-using long-lived connections.
Reject RST in TIME_WAIT (avoids the rare race in RFC 1337).
1 = stop responding to ICMP echo (ping). Hardening for hosts that don't want to be pingable.
1 = ignore broadcast ping (Smurf attack mitigation).
Reverse path filter. 1 = strict (drop packets if return path doesn't match arrival interface — RFC 3704). 2 = loose. 0 = off. Container/VM hosts often need 2 or 0 for asymmetric routing.
Accept ICMP redirects (router can tell host of better next-hop). 0 = ignore (security hardening; routers/NAT boxes always 0).
Send ICMP redirects when this host routes a packet that would have been better sent direct. 0 = silent (most non-router hosts).
Reply to ARP requests for any local IP (0) vs only if target IP is on the receiving interface (1). Important for multi-homed hosts to avoid wrong-interface-replies.
Source IP selection for outgoing ARP requests. 2 = always use the IP on the announcing interface (avoids leaking other-interface IPs).
Respond to ARP for IPs on other interfaces. Used in some bridging/routing setups.
1 = disable Path MTU Discovery system-wide (don't set DF bit). Workaround for broken intermediate ICMP filtering.
Default TTL for outgoing IPv4 packets.
List of compiled-in congestion control algorithms.
Algorithms unprivileged users can select per-socket via TCP_CONGESTION.
Limit unsent bytes in send queue when EPOLLOUT triggers. Helps app-layer paced sending. Per-socket: TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT.
Explicit Congestion Notification. 0=off, 1=on, 2=passive (advertise but don't initiate).
Hint to kernel to favor latency over throughput in scheduling decisions.
1 = disable IPv6 on all interfaces. Persistent disable: also set in sysctl.d. Better to set per-interface if some need IPv6.
Enable IPv6 forwarding (router functionality).
Accept Router Advertisement. 2 = accept even with forwarding=1 (otherwise RAs ignored on routers).
SLAAC (stateless autoconfig) on/off.
RFC 4941 privacy temp addresses. 0 = off, 1 = generate but don't prefer, 2 = generate and prefer.
Accept source-routed packets. 0 = drop (security default).
0 = AF_INET6 socket also accepts v4 (mapped). 1 = v6-only by default. Per-socket override IPV6_V6ONLY.
Min ms between ICMPv6 error messages (rate limit).
Max IPv6 routing cache entries.
Hard ceiling on listen() backlog. App requests min(app, somaxconn). Raise on heavy connection-rate servers.
Per-CPU max packets queued from NIC to softnet (between IRQ and IP stack). Drops here visible in /proc/net/softnet_stat. Raise on 10G+ NICs.
Max value SO_RCVBUF can be set to. Raise to allow apps to set larger buffers (typical: 16777216).
Max value SO_SNDBUF can be set to.
Default SO_RCVBUF for new sockets (non-TCP — TCP uses tcp_rmem auto-tune).
Default SO_SNDBUF.
Max ancillary buffer per socket (for SCM_RIGHTS, IP_PKTINFO, etc.).
BPF JIT compilation. 1 = on, 2 = on + log to kernel ring buffer.
BPF JIT hardening (constant blinding) against spectre-style attacks. 1 = unprivileged users only, 2 = all.
Poll-mode socket recv (low latency at cost of CPU). Per-socket: SO_BUSY_POLL.
Same as busy_poll but for socket read.
Default queueing discipline assigned to new interfaces. fq_codel is bufferbloat-resistant; bbr congestion control wants fq.
Max connection-tracking entries. Hitting it = `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` in dmesg, new conns drop. Raise on busy NAT/firewall hosts.
Conntrack hash table bucket count. Set to nf_conntrack_max/4 typically. Boot-time only on some kernels.

How long ESTABLISHED entries persist without traffic. Long-lived TCP through stateful FW must use TCP keepalive shorter than this OR firewall will silently lose state, killing the conn on next packet.
TIME_WAIT timeout in conntrack.
CLOSE_WAIT timeout.
FIN_WAIT timeout.
SYN_SENT timeout.
UDP unidirectional timeout (seen one direction only).
UDP bidirectional (assumed stream) timeout. e.g. DNS round-trip.
ICMP timeout.
Catch-all for protocols without specific timeout.
Verify packet checksum before tracking.
Auto-load conntrack ALG helpers (FTP, SIP, TFTP, IRC). 0 = require explicit loading (security default since 4.7).
Per-flow byte/packet counters. Doubles conntrack entry size.
Log packets that fail conntrack validation. 6 = TCP, 17 = UDP, 1 = ICMP, 255 = all.
Allow bind() to address still in TIME_WAIT, or to wildcard when specific is bound (and vice versa).
Allow MULTIPLE listeners on same address+port; kernel hashes incoming connections across them. The way to scale accept() across CPU cores.
Enable TCP keepalive on this socket. Defaults from net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_*.

On close(), if linger.l_onoff && data queued: block up to l_linger seconds. l_linger=0 → RST instead of FIN (immediate close, no TIME_WAIT — useful for short-lived clients but discards in-flight data).
Receive buffer size. Setting disables TCP auto-tuning. Cap by net.core.rmem_max.
Send buffer size.
Per-socket recv timeout. recv() returns EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK after this elapses.
Per-socket send timeout.
Allow sendto() to broadcast addresses (UDP only). Required for DHCP clients, etc.
Pending socket-level error. Reading clears it. Used after non-blocking connect() to retrieve actual error.
Socket type (SOCK_STREAM/DGRAM/SEQPACKET/RAW). Useful for libraries given a generic FD.
Bind socket to specific interface. Requires CAP_NET_RAW. Used by VPN clients to send out a tunnel.
Set fwmark on outgoing packets. Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN. Used by policy routing.
Receive SCM_CREDENTIALS ancillary data with each message (PID/UID/GID of sender). AF_UNIX only.
Get credentials of peer process at connect time. AF_UNIX. The mechanism systemd uses to identify clients on /run/systemd/private.
Sets skb->priority for tc qdisc selection. CAP_NET_ADMIN for >6.
Per-socket busy-polling for low-latency reads.
Hint kernel which CPU should handle this socket's RX (RFS/XPS coordination).
Disable Nagle's algorithm. Send writes immediately. Latency-critical apps.
Coalesce sends until uncorked. Linux-specific. Pairs with sendfile(2) for header+body.
Per-socket override of net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time.
Per-socket interval between keepalive probes.
Per-socket failed-probe count before reset.
Max segment size hint. Set before connect() to advertise smaller MSS.
Disable delayed ACKs (immediately ACK on read). Latency-helpful, throughput-hurtful. Reset to 0 after each packet.
Don't return from accept() until data arrives (or N seconds pass). Saves a wakeup on protocols where client speaks first (HTTP).
Per-socket override of tcp_syn_retries.
Per-connection TCP state: cwnd, ssthresh, rtt, retransmits, etc. ss -ti uses this.
Per-socket congestion control algorithm name.
Server-side: backlog of TFO-pending connections.
Client-side: enable TFO for next connect().
Override default tcp_retries2 with explicit ms timeout for unACKed data.
Per-socket NOTSENT low-water mark for EPOLLOUT.
1 = AF_INET6 socket binds only IPv6 (no v4-mapped).
Receive in_pktinfo ancillary data (which interface, dst addr).
Multicast TTL for outgoing v6 multicast.
Unicast TTL for outgoing v6.
Loop multicast back to local sender.
Join multicast group on specified interface.
Traffic class (DSCP) for outgoing v6.
Allow packet, end traversal of current chain.
Silently discard packet. Sender sees a black hole (timeout).
Drop and send ICMP/RST back. Polite alternative to DROP — sender knows immediately. --reject-with: icmp-port-unreachable (default), icmp-net-unreachable, tcp-reset, etc.
Log packet to kernel ring buffer (dmesg/journald). Doesn't terminate traversal — packet continues to next rule.
Return from user-defined chain to caller. In built-in chain = use chain's default policy.
Source NAT — rewrite source IP/port of outbound packets. POSTROUTING only. e.g. --to-source 1.2.3.4 or range 1.2.3.4-1.2.3.10.
Destination NAT — rewrite dest IP/port. PREROUTING (or OUTPUT for local-out). The mechanism behind `docker -p`.
Like SNAT but auto-pick source IP from outgoing interface. POSTROUTING only. The way to NAT private network behind a dynamically-assigned public IP.
DNAT to local machine. PREROUTING (or OUTPUT for local). Used by transparent proxies (incoming :80 → local :8080).
Set fwmark on packet. mangle table. Used with policy routing (`ip rule fwmark X`).
Clamp TCP MSS option. mangle FORWARD chain. Common workaround for MTU-mismatch on PPPoE/tunnel uplinks.
Match protocol: tcp|udp|icmp|esp|ah|sctp|all|<num>.
Match source IP.
Match destination IP.
Match input interface (PREROUTING/INPUT/FORWARD).
Match output interface (FORWARD/OUTPUT/POSTROUTING).
Source port (tcp/udp). Range with colon.
Destination port (tcp/udp).
Conntrack state match. The cornerstone of stateful firewalls.
Modern equivalent of -m state. Superset of state matches; also --ctorigsrc, --ctorigdst, --ctstatus.
Match specific TCP flags. e.g. `--tcp-flags ALL SYN` = SYN-only (no other flags) packets.
Shorthand for --tcp-flags SYN,RST,ACK SYN — matches new TCP connection attempts.
e.g. --icmp-type echo-request. iptables -p icmp -h lists names.
Match multiple ports in one rule (up to 15).
Token-bucket rate limit. e.g. --limit 5/sec. --limit-burst sets burst size.
Per-IP rate limiting / temporary blocklist. Used for SSH brute-force protection.
Match by sending process UID. OUTPUT only. Used for per-user firewall rules.
Match fwmark.
Match physical interface (when bridged). Useful for FORWARD rules on br_netfilter setups.
Unified IPv4+IPv6. Modern default — write rules once, applies to both. e.g. `add table inet filter`.
IPv4 only.
IPv6 only.
ARP packets.
Bridge family — runs at L2 within Linux bridge.
Per-interface ingress/egress at the lowest level (before/after the rest of netfilter). Useful for early-drop.
IPv4 source address. Supports CIDR, ranges, named sets.
IPv4 dest address.
IPv6 source.
IPv6 dest.
TCP destination port. e.g. `tcp dport { 22, 80, 443 }` matches any of those.
TCP source port.
UDP destination port.
TCP flags. e.g. `tcp flags syn` matches SYN-set packets.
ICMP message type. e.g. `icmp type echo-request`.
Conntrack state. e.g. `ct state established,related accept`.
Conntrack mark.
Input interface.
Output interface.
skb fwmark.
skb priority (for tc).
Cgroup ID of sending process. Per-cgroup firewall rules.
Match packets to/from host. Combine with src/dst: `src host 1.2.3.4`.
Source or destination port. `port 80` matches both directions.
Restrict next host/port to source side.
Restrict next host/port to dest side.
Match TCP packets.
Match UDP packets.
Match ICMPv4.
Match ICMPv6.
Match CIDR network. e.g. `net 192.168.1.0/24`.
Match IP protocol number/name.
L2 — `ether host MAC`, `ether broadcast`, `ether multicast`, `ether proto`.
Match VLAN-tagged frames. Optional ID: `vlan 10`.
Bit-mask access to TCP flags. e.g. `tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0` (SYN set).
Packet length filter: `greater 1500`.
Packet length filter: `less 64`.
DNS server IP. Up to 3 (MAXNS); used in order. e.g. `nameserver 8.8.8.8`.
Domain search list. Names with fewer dots than `ndots` get search-list suffixes appended. Up to 6 domains.
Local domain. Single-element search list (deprecated; use search).
Threshold for relative-vs-absolute lookup. Kubernetes default ndots:5.
Per-query timeout.
Resend attempts before giving up.
Round-robin nameservers (vs always start at first).
Send A and AAAA queries serially (vs concurrent). Workaround for buggy DNS servers.
Use separate sockets for A and AAAA. Avoids race in some setups.
Enable EDNS0 (larger UDP responses).
Pass the AD (authenticated data) bit through to applications.
Source(s) for getpwnam/getpwuid. e.g. `passwd: files systemd ldap`.
Source(s) for getgrnam/getgrgid.
Source(s) for getaddrinfo. e.g. `hosts: files mdns_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] resolve [!UNAVAIL=return] dns`. Order matters.
Source(s) for getnetbyname.
Source(s) for getservbyname (port ↔ service name).
Source(s) for getprotobyname (proto ↔ number).
Source for shadow passwords.
Source for netgroups (NIS/NIS+).
Mail aliases.
Source for initgroups (supplementary GIDs).
Interfaces, addresses, routes, neighbours, qdiscs, filters. The thing `ip` and `tc` use.
nftables, conntrack, ulogd.
Linux audit subsystem (auditd talks here).
Generic netlink — multiplexed family for new subsystems (devlink, l2tp, taskstats, drm, fou, etc.).
Kernel ↔ udev events (device hotplug).
Old netfilter packet queueing. Largely superseded by NFQUEUE.
Data available to read.
Buffer space available to write.
Error condition. Always reported (don't need to register).
Hang up. Always reported.
Peer half-closed (FIN received). Useful to detect disconnect without consuming all data first.
Edge-triggered. Event reported once per state change.
After event delivery, FD is disabled until rearmed via EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
Wake only one waiter (avoid thundering herd when multiple epoll_wait()ers monitor the same FD).
Socket-layer options (SO_*).
TCP-layer options (TCP_*).
UDP-layer options (UDP_*).
IPv4 options (IP_*).
IPv6 options (IPV6_*).
Per-line host entry. e.g. `127.0.0.1 localhost`. Tab or space separated. Consulted by glibc when nsswitch hosts has 'files' before 'dns'.
# starts a comment to end-of-line.
When 1, bridged packets traverse iptables FORWARD. The mechanism behind container-traffic firewalling on docker0. Some kubernetes setups require this.
Same for IPv6.
ARP-level. Rarely needed.
Filter VLAN-tagged frames at iptables level.
